recipe_version.title: Japchae: Korean Sweet Potato Glass Noodles with Vegetables and Shiitake
recipe_version.description: Chewy sweet potato glass noodles tossed with stir-fried onion, carrot, red bell pepper, shiitake, and scallions plus blanched spinach in a garlicky sesame-soy sauce, finished with toasted sesame seeds.

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Thinly slice the onion, julienne the carrots, cut the pepper into strips, slice the shiitake caps, cut the scallions, and mince the garlic. In the large bowl stir the soy sauce, sugar, 2 tbsp of the sesame oil, the garlic, and the black pepper.

steps.title: Heat the noodle pot
steps.body: Fill a 6-quart pot with 12 cups water, cover, and set it over high heat. It takes about 12 minutes to come to a boil, which runs inside steps 3 and 4 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
steps.body: Heat 1 tbsp neutral oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Stir-fry the onion and carrot with 1/4 tsp salt until crisp-tender, about 3 minutes, and add them to the sauce bowl. Add 1 tbsp oil and stir-fry the pepper about 2 minutes; add to the bowl. Add the last 1 tbsp oil and stir-fry the shiitake until browned, about 3 minutes, adding the scallions for the last minute; add to the bowl.

steps.title: Toast the sesame seeds
steps.body: Wipe the skillet, set it over medium, and toast the sesame seeds, shaking the pan, until golden, about 2 minutes. Tip them onto a plate.

steps.title: Blanch the spinach and cook the noodles
steps.body: Drop the spinach into the boiling pot for 30 seconds, lift it out with tongs, cool it under the cold tap, squeeze it dry, and add it to the bowl with 1/4 tsp salt. Add the noodles to the same pot and boil until chewy and translucent, 6 to 7 minutes. Drain in the colander, rinse briefly under the cold tap, drain well, and snip them two or three times with scissors.

steps.title: Toss
steps.body: Add the noodles and the remaining 1 tbsp sesame oil to the bowl and toss with tongs until the noodles are evenly glossy and the vegetables are spread through. Taste and add the last 1/4 tsp salt if needed.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Pile onto a platter and scatter the sesame seeds over.
